answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce stake before submitting work, then slash it when independently verified fraud is proven. Creating a prism of aliases does not multiply influence: every identity needs its own capital, and linked claims can reveal shared funding. The attacker's cost grows in a spiral as more stake is tied up and exposed to loss. A marble-sized deposit will not deter a well-funded attacker, so the stake must exceed likely gains.
